facts.quote: growing up to 8 - 9 m in length and weighing 1.7 - 3.0 MT

facts.statement: The discovery of 26 individuals at one site provides evidence that Albertosaurus exhibited gregarious behavior.
facts.quote: The discovery of 26 individuals in one particular site provides evidence of gregarious behavior

facts.statement: Albertosaurus was named by Henry Fairfield Osborn in 1905.
facts.quote: named by Henry Fairfield Osborn in a one-page note at the end of his 1905 description of Tyrannosaurus

facts.statement: The genus name Albertosaurus refers to the Canadian province of Alberta, where the first remains were found in the same year the name was coined.
facts.quote: Its namesake is Alberta, the Canadian province established the very same year where the first remains were found

facts.statement: The specific name sarcophagus is derived from the Ancient Greek word meaning "flesh-eating".
facts.quote: The type species is Albertosaurus sarcophagus and the specific name is derived from the Ancient Greek term σαρκοφάγος (), meaning "flesh-eating"

facts.statement: The type specimen, a partial skull, was collected on June 9, 1884, from the Horseshoe Canyon Formation near the Red Deer River in Alberta.
facts.quote: The type specimen is a partial skull collected on June 9, 1884, from an outcrop of the Horseshoe Canyon Formation alongside the Red Deer River in Alberta

facts.statement: The type specimen was recovered by an expedition led by geologist Joseph Burr Tyrrell.
facts.quote: It was recovered by an expedition of the Geological Survey of Canada, led by the famous geologist Joseph Burr Tyrrell

facts.statement: Henry Fairfield Osborn named the species Albertosaurus sarcophagus in 1905.
facts.quote: Osborn gave them the new name Albertosaurus sarcophagus in 1905

facts.statement: In 2010, Thomas Carr confirmed that Albertosaurus is a valid taxon by identifying a unique trait shared by the holotype, paratype, and later finds.
facts.quote: in 2010, Thomas Carr established that the holotype, the paratype, and comparable later finds all shared a single common unique trait, or autapomorphy

facts.statement: Barnum Brown discovered a large group of Albertosaurus remains on August 11, 1910, near the Red Deer River.
facts.quote: On August 11, 1910, American paleontologist Barnum Brown discovered the remains of a large group of Albertosaurus at another quarry alongside the Red Deer River

facts.statement: Excavations between 1997 and 2005 uncovered remains of 13 additional individuals, ranging from a two-year-old to an individual estimated at over 10 meters long.
facts.quote: Further excavation from 1997 to 2005 turned up the remains of 13 more individuals of various ages, including a diminutive two-year-old and a very old individual estimated at over 10 m long

facts.statement: William Parks described the species Albertosaurus arctunguis in 1928.
facts.quote: William Parks described a new species in 1928, Albertosaurus arctunguis

facts.quote: Specimen RTMP 81.010.001 was found in 1978 by amateur paleontologist Maurice Stefanuk

facts.statement: Two specimens tentatively identified as Albertosaurus have been found in the Packard and Corral de Enmedio Formations in Mexico.
facts.quote: Two specimens from "cf Albertosaurus ".sp" have been found in Mexico (Packard Formation and Corral de Enmedio Formation)

facts.statement: Scientists disagree on the classification of the genus, with some recognizing Gorgosaurus libratus as a distinct species separate from Albertosaurus.
facts.quote: Scientists disagree on the content of the genus and some recognize Gorgosaurus libratus as a second species

facts.statement: Fossils reported from Montana, New Mexico, Wyoming, and Missouri are doubted to belong to A. sarcophagus and may not belong to the genus Albertosaurus at all.

facts.statement: Charles H. Sternberg recovered an Albertosaurus skeleton in Alberta in 1913.
facts.quote: In 1913, paleontologist Charles H. Sternberg recovered another tyrannosaurid skeleton from the slightly older Dinosaur Park Formation in Alberta.

facts.statement: Lawrence Lambe originally named the species Gorgosaurus libratus in 1914.
facts.quote: Lawrence Lambe named this dinosaur Gorgosaurus libratus in 1914.

facts.statement: Dale Russell renamed Gorgosaurus libratus to Albertosaurus libratus in 1970, declaring Gorgosaurus a junior synonym.
facts.quote: Dale Russell declared the name Gorgosaurus a junior synonym of Albertosaurus, which had been named first, and G. libratus was renamed Albertosaurus libratus in 1970.

facts.statement: Several Albertosaurus specimens have been recovered from Alaska and New Mexico.
facts.quote: In addition to this, several albertosaurine specimens have been recovered from Alaska and New Mexico.

facts.statement: Anatoly Nikolaevich Riabinin named Albertosaurus pericolosus in 1930 based on a Chinese tooth now thought to belong to Tarbosaurus.
facts.quote: In 1930, Anatoly Nikolaevich Riabinin named Albertosaurus pericolosus based on a tooth from China that probably belonged to Tarbosaurus.

facts.statement: Gregory S. Paul described Albertosaurus megagracilis in 1988 based on specimen LACM 28345 from Montana.
facts.quote: In 1988, Gregory S. Paul based Albertosaurus megagracilis on a small tyrannosaurid skeleton, specimen LACM 28345, from the Hell Creek Formation of Montana.

facts.statement: Bryn Mader and Robert Bradley renamed Gorgosaurus novojilovi to Albertosaurus novojilovi in 1989.
facts.quote: In 1989, Gorgosaurus novojilovi (Maleev 1955) was renamed by Bryn Mader and Robert Bradley as Albertosaurus novojilovi.

facts.statement: Adult Albertosaurus measured up to 8 to 9 meters long and weighed between 1.7 and 3.0 metric tons.
facts.quote: Typical Albertosaurus adults measured up to 8 - 9 m long and weighed between 1.7 and 3.0 MT in body mass.

facts.statement: Albertosaurus had long legs ending in a four-toed foot where the first toe was very short and did not touch the ground.
facts.quote: The legs were long and ended in a four-toed foot on which the first toe, the hallux, was very short and did not reach the ground.

facts.statement: Albertosaurus could likely walk at speeds between 14 and 21 kilometers per hour.
facts.quote: Albertosaurus may have been able to reach walking speeds of 14–21 km/hour (8–13 mi/hour).

facts.statement: A skin impression from Albertosaurus found near gastralic ribs indicates it came from the belly.
facts.quote: One patch was found associated with some gastralic ribs and the impression of a long, unknown bone, indicating that the patch is from the belly.

facts.statement: Albertosaurus belly scales were pebbly and gradually became larger and somewhat hexagonal.
facts.quote: The scales are pebbly and gradually become larger and somewhat hexagonal in shape.

facts.statement: Albertosaurus is one of only two known theropods, along with Carnotaurus, to have preserved feature scales.
facts.quote: making Albertosaurus, along with Carnotaurus, the only known theropods with preserved feature scales.

facts.statement: Albertosaurus had small, diamond-shaped scales arranged in rows on an unknown body part.
facts.quote: These scales are small, diamond-shaped, and arranged in rows.

facts.statement: The largest adult Albertosaurus had a massive skull about 1 meter long perched on a short, S-shaped neck.
facts.quote: The massive skull of Albertosaurus, which was perched on a muscular, short, S-shaped neck, was about 1 m long in the largest adults.

facts.statement: Albertosaurus long jaws contained 58 or more banana-shaped teeth in total on both sides.
facts.quote: Its long jaws contained, both sides combined, 58 or more banana-shaped teeth.

facts.statement: The four premaxillary teeth at the tip of each upper jaw were smaller, closely packed, and D-shaped in cross-section.
facts.quote: The premaxillary teeth at the tip of the upper jaw, four per side, were much smaller than the rest, more closely packed, and D-shaped in cross section.

facts.statement: The maximum bite force of Albertosaurus by the back teeth reached 3,413 Newtons.
facts.quote: the maximum force, by the back teeth, reaching 3,413 Newtons.

facts.statement: Short bony crests above Albertosaurus eyes may have been brightly colored and used by males for courtship.
facts.quote: Above the eyes were short bony crests that may have been brightly coloured in life and possibly used, by males in particular, in courtship to attract a mate.

facts.statement: William Abler observed in 2001 that Albertosaurus tooth serrations ended in a round void called an ampulla.
facts.quote: In 2001, William Abler observed that Albertosaurus tooth serrations resemble a crack in the tooth ending in a round void called an ampulla.

facts.statement: Experiments showed that teeth with ampullas were more than 25% stronger than those without, similar to engineering techniques used in aircraft.
facts.quote: Abler demonstrated that a plexiglass bar with incisions called "kerfs" and drilled holes was more than 25% stronger than one with only regularly placed incisions.

facts.statement: Albertosaurus belongs to the theropod family Tyrannosauridae and the subfamily Albertosaurinae.
facts.quote: Albertosaurus is a member of the theropod family Tyrannosauridae, specifically the subfamily Albertosaurinae.

facts.statement: The closest relative of Albertosaurus is the slightly older Gorgosaurus libratus.
facts.quote: Its closest relative is the slightly older Gorgosaurus libratus (sometimes called Albertosaurus libratus; see below).

facts.statement: Thomas Holtz initially classified Appalachiosaurus as an albertosaurine in 2004, but later placed it outside Tyrannosauridae in agreement with other authors.
facts.quote: Thomas Holtz found Appalachiosaurus to be an albertosaurine in 2004, but his more recent unpublished work places it as a basal eotyrannosaurian just outside of Tyrannosauridae, in agreement with other authors.

facts.statement: Albertosaurines like Albertosaurus had slender builds with smaller skulls and longer lower leg and foot bones compared to tyrannosaurines.
facts.quote: Compared with the more robust tyrannosaurines, albertosaurines had slender builds, with proportionately smaller skulls and longer bones of the lower legs (tibia) and feet (metatarsals and phalanges).

facts.statement: The youngest known Albertosaurus fossil is a two-year-old individual found in the Dry Island bonebed that weighed approximately 50 kilograms and measured slightly over 2 meters in length.
facts.quote: The youngest known Albertosaurus is a two-year-old discovered in the Dry Island bonebed, which would have weighed about 50 kilograms (110 lb) and measured slightly more than 2 m long.

facts.statement: A 10-meter-long specimen from the Dry Island bonebed is 28 years old, representing the oldest and largest known Albertosaurus.
facts.quote: The 10 m specimen from the same quarry is 28 years old, the oldest and largest one known.

facts.statement: Based on an estimated adult weight of 1.3 tonnes, the rapid growth phase of Albertosaurus occurred at a rate of 122 kilograms per year.
facts.quote: The growth rate during this phase was 122 kg per year, based on an adult weighing 1.3 tonnes.

facts.statement: Researchers suggest that the end of Albertosaurus's rapid growth phase indicates the onset of sexual maturity, though growth continued at a slower rate for the rest of their lives.
facts.quote: The end of the rapid growth phase suggests the onset of sexual maturity in Albertosaurus, although growth continued at a slower rate throughout the animals' lives.

facts.statement: Most known Albertosaurus fossils represent individuals that were at least 14 years old when they died.
facts.quote: Most known Albertosaurus individuals were aged 14 years or older at the time of death.

facts.statement: By the age of two, juvenile Albertosaurus were larger than any other regional predator besides adults and faster than most of their prey.
facts.quote: After just two years, juveniles were larger than any other predator in the region, aside from adult Albertosaurus, and more fleet-footed than most of their prey animals.

facts.statement: Albertosaurus mortality rates reportedly doubled at age twelve and again between ages fourteen and sixteen, coinciding with rapid growth and sexual maturity.
facts.quote: Mortality rates doubled at age twelve, perhaps the result of the physiological demands of the rapid growth phase, and then doubled again with the onset of sexual maturity between the ages of fourteen and sixteen.

facts.statement: The Dry Island bonebed, discovered by Barnum Brown, contains 26 Albertosaurus specimens, the largest single assemblage of any large Cretaceous theropod and the second-largest of any large theropod dinosaur.
facts.quote: The Dry Island bonebed discovered by Barnum Brown and his crew contains the remains of 26 Albertosaurus, the most individuals found in one locality of any large Cretaceous theropod and the second-most of any large theropod dinosaur behind the Allosaurus assemblage at the Cleveland-Lloyd Dinosaur Quarry in Utah.

facts.statement: The Dry Island bonebed assemblage includes one very old adult, eight adults aged 17 to 23, seven sub-adults aged 12 to 16, and six juveniles aged 2 to 11.
facts.quote: The group seems to be composed of one very old adult, eight adults between 17 and 23 years old, seven sub-adults undergoing their rapid growth phases at between 12 and 16 years old, and six juveniles between the ages of 2 and 11 years old that had not yet reached the growth phase.

facts.statement: It is debated whether the Dry Island bonebed represents pack behavior or if the animals were driven together by environmental factors like drought or flood.
facts.quote: Currie claims this as evidence of pack behavior. Other scientists are skeptical, observing that the animals may have been driven together by a drought, flood, or other reasons.

facts.statement: In 2024, Coppock and Currie reported evidence of cannibalism in Albertosaurus, citing tooth traces on a pubis that likely belonged to another A. sarcophagus individual.
facts.quote: The evidence of cannibalism was later reported in 2024 by Coppock and Currie. The evidence consisted of tooth traces found on the medial surface of a pubis attributed to an albertosaurine, which given the lack of other albertosaurine species in the assemblage almost certainly reflected another A. sarcophagus.

facts.statement: Bite traces found on Albertosaurus fossils show no healing, indicating they are post-mortem feeding marks rather than injuries from combat.
facts.quote: These bite traces show no signs of healing and thus strongly indicate that they were made post-mortem and represent feeding marks as opposed to injuries sustained during intraspecific combat.

facts.statement: Currie hypothesized that younger Albertosaurus drove prey toward larger, more powerful but slower adults as part of a pack-hunting strategy.
facts.quote: Currie hypothesized that the younger members of the pack may have been responsible for driving their prey towards the adults, who were larger and more powerful, but also slower.

facts.statement: Because behavior preservation in the fossil record is rare, hypotheses about Albertosaurus social behavior cannot be readily tested.
facts.quote: However, as the preservation of behaviour in the fossil record is exceedingly rare, these ideas cannot readily be tested.

facts.statement: In 2009, researchers hypothesized that smooth-edged holes in Albertosaurus fossil jaws were caused by a bird-like parasite that may have impaired the dinosaur's ability to eat.
facts.quote: In 2009, researchers hypothesized that smooth-edged holes found in the fossil jaws of tyrannosaurid dinosaurs, such as Albertosaurus, were caused by a parasite similar to Trichomonas gallinae, which infects birds.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen ROM 807 possessed a hole measuring 2.5 by 3.5 cm deep in its iliac blade.
facts.quote: ROM 807, the holotype of A. arctunguis (now referred to A. sarcophagus), had a 2.5 by 3.5 cm deep hole in the iliac blade

facts.statement: In 1970, Dale Russel reported that two of five Albertosaurus sarcophagus specimens with humeri showed pathological damage.
facts.quote: In 1970, two of the five Albertosaurus sarcophagus specimens with humeri were reported by Dale Russel as having pathological damage to them.

facts.statement: Most Albertosaurus sarcophagus fossils are found in the upper Horseshoe Canyon Formation in Alberta.
facts.quote: Most fossils of Albertosaurus sarcophagus are known from the upper Horseshoe Canyon Formation in Alberta.

facts.statement: Albertosaurus lived during the early Maastrichtian age of the Late Cretaceous, approximately 70 to 68 million years ago.
facts.quote: These younger units of this geologic formation date to the early Maastrichtian age of the Late Cretaceous period, about 70 to 68 million years ago.

facts.statement: Albertosaurus remains are found in river delta and floodplain deposits from the later half of the Horseshoe Canyon times.
facts.quote: Albertosaurus remains are found in deposits laid down in the deltas and floodplains of large rivers during the later half of Horseshoe Canyon times.

facts.statement: Albertosaurus is classified within the subfamily Albertosaurinae.
facts.quote: subfamilia: Albertosaurinae

facts.statement: Albertosaurus belongs to the tribe Albertosaurini.
facts.quote: tribus: Albertosaurini

facts.statement: As a tyrannosaurid, Albertosaurus was a bipedal predator with a large head, jaws holding dozens of large teeth, and small two-fingered hands.
facts.quote: Al ser un tiranosáurido, los albertosaurios fueron depredadores bípedos con una gran cabeza, mandíbulas provistas de docenas de grandes dientes y pequeñas «manos» de dos dedos.

facts.statement: Albertosaurus was much smaller than its famous relative Tyrannosaurus, likely weighing as much as a modern black rhinoceros.
facts.quote: Aunque sea relativamente grande para un terópodo, Albertosaurus era mucho más pequeño que su famoso pariente Tyrannosaurus, probablemente pesando tanto como un rinoceronte negro moderno.

facts.statement: The discovery of twenty-six individuals together at one site suggests evidence of group behavior in Albertosaurus.
facts.quote: El hallazgo de veintiséis individuos juntos en un sitio señala evidencia de comportamiento en grupos

facts.statement: Adult Albertosaurus reached approximately nine meters in length, while some older individuals may have reached ten meters.
facts.quote: Los adultos alcanzaban aproximadamente nueve metros de largo, mientras que algunos individuos, los de mayor edad, habrían alcanzado los diez metros.

facts.statement: Independent mass estimates suggest an adult Albertosaurus weighed between 1.3 and 1.7 tons, with a maximum of 2.5 tons.
facts.quote: Varias estimaciones independientes sobre su masa, obtenidas mediante diferentes métodos, sugieren que un Albertosaurus adulto habría pesado entre 1,3 y 1,7 y un máximo de 2,5 toneladas.

facts.statement: There is disagreement in the scientific community regarding the number of species in the genus, with estimates ranging from one to two species.
facts.quote: Existe cierto desacuerdo en la comunidad científica en cuanto al número de especies representadas en el género, que según el caso serían una o dos.

facts.statement: Adult Albertosaurus had a skull approximately one meter long supported by a short S-shaped neck.
facts.quote: El enorme cráneo de Albertosaurus, sostenido por un cuello corto con forma de S, medía aproximadamente un metro de largo en los adultos más grandes.

facts.statement: Albertosaurus possessed more than sixty slightly curved teeth in its long jaws, a higher count than larger tyrannosaurids.
facts.quote: Sus largas mandíbulas contenían más de sesenta dientes ligeramente curvados, muchos en comparación con los tiranosáuridos más grandes, que poseían menos dientes.

facts.statement: Tyrannosaurids, unlike most theropods, exhibited heterodont dentition where teeth varied in shape based on their position in the mouth.
facts.quote: A diferencia de la mayoría de terópodos, los tiranosáuridos tenían dentición heterodonta, es decir, los dientes presentaban diferentes formas dependiendo de su posición en la boca.

facts.statement: The premaxillary teeth at the front of the upper jaw were much smaller, compact, and D-shaped in cross-section.
facts.quote: Los dientes premaxilares, en el extremo del maxilar superior, eran mucho más pequeños que el resto, compactos y con sección en forma de D.

facts.statement: The maximum bite force exerted by the posterior teeth of Albertosaurus reached 3,413 newtons.
facts.quote: La fuerza máxima ejercida por los dientes posteriores llegaba a 3413 newton.

facts.statement: In 2001, William Abler observed that the striations on Albertosaurus teeth were so fine they could functionally act as a crack in the tooth.
facts.quote: William Abler observó en 2001 que las estrías de los dientes de Albertosaurus son tan finas que pueden ser funcionalmente una grieta en el diente.

facts.statement: A round hollow space called an ampulla at the base of the tooth striations helped distribute forces over a larger surface area, preventing cracks from propagating through the tooth.
facts.quote: En la base de esta grieta hay un espacio vacío redondo llamado ampolla que funcionaba para distribuir las fuerzas sobre una mayor área de superficie, lo que dificultaba la capacidad de la «grieta» formada por el dentado de propagarse a través del diente.

facts.statement: Tyrannosaurid teeth were used as anchoring discs to pull meat from a carcass rather than functioning as knives for cutting.
facts.quote: Los dientes de los tiranosáuridos fueron usados como discos de fijación para tirar de la carne de un cuerpo, en vez de funcionar como cuchillos que efectúan un corte.

facts.statement: Wear patterns on the teeth suggest that head-shaking behavior may have been involved in tyrannosaurid feeding.
facts.quote: Los patrones de desgaste de los dientes insinúan que el comportamiento de sacudir la cabeza puede haber estado involucrado en la alimentación de los tiranosáuridos.

facts.statement: The first Albertosaurus was discovered by Joseph Burr Tyrrell during geological prospecting in 1884.
facts.quote: El primer Albertosaurus fue encontrado por Joseph Burr Tyrrell durante unas prospecciones geológicas en 1884.

facts.statement: Albertosaurus was named in 1905 by Henry Fairfield Osborn of the American Museum of Natural History in a brief note at the end of his description of Tyrannosaurus rex.
facts.quote: Albertosaurus fue nombrado en 1905 por Henry Fairfield Osborn, del Museo Americano de Historia Natural, en una muy breve nota al final de su descripción de Tyrannosaurus rex.

facts.statement: The name Albertosaurus honors the Canadian province of Alberta, where the first remains were found.
facts.quote: El nombre hace honor a Alberta, la provincia canadiense en la cual se encontraron los primeros restos.

facts.statement: More than thirty specimens of various ages are known for Albertosaurus.
facts.quote: Se conocen más de treinta especímenes de diversas edades.

facts.statement: A two-year-old Albertosaurus fossil, the youngest found to date, was discovered at Dry Island weighing approximately fifty kilograms and measuring two meters long.
facts.quote: Recientemente ha sido hallado un fósil de Albertosaurus de dos años de edad, el más joven hallado hasta el momento, en la cama de huesos de Dry Island que ha sido reabierta, que debió pesar cerca de cincuenta kilogramos y medir dos metros de largo.

facts.statement: The oldest specimen from the same quarry was approximately twenty-eight years old and about ten meters long.
facts.quote: Otro espécimen de la misma cantera es el más viejo, de alrededor de veintiocho años de edad y unos diez metros de largo.

facts.statement: A twenty-four-year-old specimen in the Tyrrell Museum of Paleontology collection would have weighed approximately 1.14 tons.
facts.quote: Un espécimen de veinticuatro años de edad de la colección del Museo Tyrrell de Paleontología habría pesado aproximadamente 1,14 toneladas.

facts.statement: An individual weighing 1.28 tons in the American Museum of Natural History collection was twenty-two years old when it died.
facts.quote: Otro individuo de 1,28 toneladas, que se encuentra en la colección del Museo Americano de Historia Natural, tenía veintidós años de edad cuando murió.

facts.statement: Albertosaurus appears to reach skeletal maturity at sixteen years of age, which coincided with the end of rapid growth and likely sexual maturity.
facts.quote: Albertosaurus parece alcanzar la madurez esquelética a los dieciséis años de edad; la misma está marcada por el fin de la fase de rápido crecimiento, que al parecer también era la edad donde alcanzaba su madurez sexual.

facts.statement: The growth rate during the rapid growth phase is estimated at an increase of 122 kg per year.
facts.quote: La tasa de crecimiento durante esta fase se estima en un aumento de 122 kg por año.

facts.statement: Small bony crests above the eyes may have been brightly colored in life and used in courtship to attract mates, though this is a hypothesis.
facts.quote: Por encima de los ojos tenía pequeñas crestas óseas que pueden haber tenido un color brillante en vida y ser utilizadas en el cortejo para atraer a su pareja.

facts.statement: This bone bed holds the largest number of individuals found at a single location of any large Cretaceous theropod.
facts.quote: la mayor cantidad de individuos encontrados en una localización de cualquier terópodo grande del Cretácico

facts.statement: Currie hypothesized that younger pack members might have driven prey toward larger, stronger, but slower adults.
facts.quote: Currie sugirió que los miembros más jóvenes de la manada podrían ser los responsables de conducir la presa hacia los adultos, que eran más grandes y fuertes, pero también más lentos

facts.statement: The leg proportions of smaller individuals are comparable to ornithomimids, which were likely among the fastest dinosaurs.
facts.quote: Las proporciones de las extremidades inferiores de los individuos más pequeños son comparables con las de los ornitomímidos, los cuales estuvieron probablemente entre los dinosaurios más veloces

facts.statement: Some researchers speculate that instead of social groups, these findings represent a feeding frenzy similar to modern Komodo dragons on dead cattle.
facts.quote: Otros han especulado que en vez de grupos sociales, por lo menos algunos de estos hallazgos representan un caso de frenesí alimentario similar a los de los dragones de Komodo sobre reses muertas

facts.statement: Albertosaurus lived from the Santonian to the Maastrichtian, between 85.7 and 66 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Santonian to Maastrichtian (85.7 to 66 million years ago)

facts.statement: Albertosaurus belongs to the parent group Albertosaurinae.
facts.quote: Parent group: Albertosaurinae

facts.quote: Family: Tyrannosauridae

facts.statement: Albertosaurus is classified as a reptile.
facts.quote: Class: Reptilia

facts.quote: PBDB name: Albertosaurus (genus), Osborn 1905

facts.quote: Evidence of preservation of micro- and nanoscale histological features (including Haversian canal and lacunocanalicular network permineralization) in bones of Albertosaurus sarcophagus from the Horseshoe Canyon Formation (Alberta, Canada) is presented by Williams et al. (2026).
